HC-SA-001.objective: Audit renal-dosing adjustments for a CKD patient on multiple medications.
HC-SA-001.opening_summary: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Patient with chronic kidney disease stage 3b presenting for medication review. Current eGFR 32 mL/min. On metformin, lisinopril, and gabapentin.
HC-SA-001.correct_diagnosis: Renal dose adjustment needed for gabapentin and metformin reassessment

histories.medications: MEDICATION-HISTORY: Metformin 1000mg BID, Lisinopril 20mg daily, Gabapentin 600mg TID, Amlodipine 5mg daily.
histories.present_illness: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Patient reports increased fatigue and occasional dizziness over past 2 weeks. No new symptoms.

physical_exams.general_exam: EXAM-FINDING: BP 138/82, HR 72, BMI 28.4. Mild bilateral ankle edema.

renal_function.summary: LAB-DETAIL: eGFR 32 mL/min, BUN 38, Creatinine 2.1, K+ 4.8 mEq/L. HbA1c 7.2%.

nephrology.default_question: Are current medications appropriately dosed for CKD stage 3b?
nephrology.impression: Gabapentin requires dose reduction to 300mg BID for eGFR <40. Metformin acceptable but monitor closely. Continue lisinopril for renoprotection.
nephrology.recommended_next_step: Adjust gabapentin, recheck eGFR in 4 weeks.

HC-SA-002.objective: Triage three simultaneous ED presentations and assign priority levels.
HC-SA-002.opening_summary: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Patient A: 55M chest pain radiating to left arm. Patient B: 22F ankle sprain. Patient C: 45M severe headache with neck stiffness.
HC-SA-002.correct_diagnosis: Patient A: possible STEMI (ESI-1), Patient C: possible meningitis (ESI-2), Patient B: musculoskeletal (ESI-4)
HC-SA-002.recommended_service: Cardiology for A, Neurology/ID for C, Orthopedics for B
HC-SA-002.urgency: Patient A immediate, Patient C urgent, Patient B non-urgent

histories.patient_a: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: 55M, chest pain 30 min onset, radiating to left arm, diaphoretic, history of hypertension.
histories.patient_b: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: 22F, twisted ankle during basketball 2 hours ago, partial weight bearing.
histories.patient_c: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: 45M, thunderclap headache 4 hours ago, neck stiffness, fever 39.2C, photophobia.

physical_exams.patient_a_exam: EXAM-FINDING: BP 160/95, HR 110, diaphoretic, S4 gallop. ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III, aVF.
physical_exams.patient_b_exam: EXAM-FINDING: Lateral ankle swelling, tenderness over ATFL, positive anterior drawer.
physical_exams.patient_c_exam: EXAM-FINDING: T 39.2C, HR 95, positive Kernig and Brudzinski signs.

patient_a_cardiac.summary: LAB-DETAIL: Troponin I 2.8 ng/mL (elevated), CK-MB 45 U/L.

patient_c_cbc.summary: LAB-DETAIL: WBC 18,200 with left shift, CRP 145 mg/L.

HC-SA-003.objective: Review latest lab results for a type 2 diabetic patient and flag intervention needs.
HC-SA-003.opening_summary: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Patient with type 2 diabetes on metformin and empagliflozin. Scheduled 3-month follow-up.
HC-SA-003.correct_diagnosis: Suboptimal glycemic control requiring medication adjustment

histories.medications: MEDICATION-HISTORY: Metformin 1000mg BID, Empagliflozin 10mg daily, Atorvastatin 20mg daily, Losartan 50mg daily.
histories.present_illness: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Increased thirst and nocturia over past month. No weight loss. Adherent to medications.

physical_exams.general_exam: EXAM-FINDING: BP 128/78, HR 76, BMI 31.2. No peripheral neuropathy. Foot exam unremarkable.

metabolic_panel.summary: LAB-DETAIL: HbA1c 8.4% (up from 7.1%), Fasting glucose 186 mg/dL, eGFR 78, LDL 98 mg/dL, Triglycerides 210 mg/dL.

endocrinology.default_question: Is medication adjustment needed given rising HbA1c?
endocrinology.impression: Consider adding a GLP-1 receptor agonist given rising HbA1c and elevated BMI.
endocrinology.recommended_next_step: Add semaglutide, recheck HbA1c in 3 months.

HC-SA-004.objective: Decide the next-line systemic regimen for a Stage IIIB EGFR-mutant NSCLC patient who has progressed on first-line osimertinib.
HC-SA-004.demographics: PATIENT-DEMOGRAPHICS: 62-year-old female, Stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma, EGFR exon 19 deletion with acquired T790M, ECOG 1.
HC-SA-004.opening_summary: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Patient referred for thoracic oncology follow-up after restaging CT showed mediastinal progression on osimertinib at 14 months. Reports new dry cough and 4 kg weight loss over 6 weeks. Performance status preserved.
HC-SA-004.correct_diagnosis: EGFR-mutant NSCLC progression on first-line osimertinib with histologic transformation; second-line platinum-doublet plus immunotherapy or amivantamab-lazertinib combination indicated pending biomarker confirmation.
HC-SA-004.recommended_service: Thoracic medical oncology with molecular tumor board review
HC-SA-004.urgency: Initiate second-line therapy within 2 weeks pending biomarker confirmation

histories.present_illness: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Restaging chest CT shows new 2.4 cm subcarinal mass and bilateral adrenal nodules. New cough and constitutional symptoms over 6 weeks.
histories.past_medical_history: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Hypertension on amlodipine; hypothyroidism on levothyroxine; remote DVT 2018 (off anticoagulation since 2019).
histories.medications: MEDICATION-HISTORY: Osimertinib 80 mg daily (since 2024-02-15), Amlodipine 5 mg daily, Levothyroxine 88 mcg daily, Vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.
histories.family_history: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Mother with stage II breast cancer at age 58 (BRCA testing pending); maternal aunt with ovarian cancer at 64.

physical_exams.general_exam: EXAM-FINDING: Temp 37.0C, BP 132/78, HR 84, SpO2 96% on room air. Mildly diminished breath sounds at the right lower base. No palpable lymphadenopathy. ECOG 1.
physical_exams.neurologic_exam: EXAM-FINDING: Cranial nerves II-XII intact. Strength 5/5 throughout. No focal deficits or meningeal signs.

tumor_marker_panel.summary: LAB-DETAIL: CEA 18.4 ng/mL (was 6.1 at baseline), CA 19-9 41 U/mL, LDH 312 U/L.

comprehensive_metabolic.summary: LAB-DETAIL: Na 138, K 4.2, Creatinine 0.9, eGFR 72, AST 32, ALT 28, total bilirubin 0.6.

thorax_abdomen_ct.summary: IMAGING-FINDING: New 2.4 cm subcarinal nodal mass and bilateral 1.1 cm adrenal nodules suspicious for metastatic disease. Stable left upper lobe primary at 1.7 cm.

brain_mri.summary: IMAGING-FINDING: No intracranial metastatic disease. No leptomeningeal enhancement.

rebiopsy_subcarinal.summary: PATHOLOGY-FINDING: Adenocarcinoma with focal small-cell transformation in approximately 30% of the specimen. EGFR exon 19 deletion retained, T790M present, MET amplification negative, PD-L1 TPS 5%.

hematology_oncology.default_question: What second-line systemic regimen is most appropriate given small-cell transformation and persistent T790M?
hematology_oncology.impression: Recommend combination platinum-doublet (carboplatin + etoposide) plus atezolizumab given partial small-cell transformation; reserve amivantamab-lazertinib for re-progression in EGFR component.
hematology_oncology.recommended_next_step: Initiate cycle 1 within 14 days; obtain echocardiogram before cycle 2; molecular tumor board for confirmation.

HC-SA-005.objective: Triage a possible subarachnoid hemorrhage presentation and determine which single imaging study is required next.
HC-SA-005.demographics: PATIENT-DEMOGRAPHICS: 38-year-old male, no prior neurosurgical history, BMI 27.
HC-SA-005.opening_summary: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Sudden-onset thunderclap headache 90 minutes ago described as the worst of his life, associated photophobia, vomited twice, no focal weakness. Arrived ambulatory, GCS 15, BP 178/102.
HC-SA-005.correct_diagnosis: Suspected subarachnoid hemorrhage; non-contrast head CT is the indicated first-line imaging within 6 hours of onset; MRI and ultrasound are not first-line and should not be ordered redundantly.
HC-SA-005.recommended_service: Emergency neurology with neurosurgery consultation if positive
HC-SA-005.urgency: Stat — image within 60 minutes of triage

histories.present_illness: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Thunderclap headache onset while lifting at the gym, peaked within 30 seconds. Photophobia and emesis x2. No fever, no recent trauma, no anticoagulation. No prior similar episodes.
histories.past_medical_history: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Hypertension diagnosed 18 months ago, intermittently treated. Smokes 0.5 pack daily.
histories.medications: MEDICATION-HISTORY: Lisinopril 10 mg daily (poor adherence). No anticoagulants. No antiplatelet agents.
histories.social_context: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Lives with partner; works as a graphic designer. Drinks alcohol socially, no recreational drug use reported.

physical_exams.general_exam: EXAM-FINDING: Temp 37.1C, BP 178/102, HR 92, RR 18, SpO2 98% on room air. Diaphoretic but well-perfused.
physical_exams.neurologic_exam: EXAM-FINDING: GCS 15. Cranial nerves II-XII intact. No pronator drift, no focal weakness. Mild neck stiffness on flexion. Photophobia present. Kernig and Brudzinski signs equivocal.

stat_basic_metabolic.summary: LAB-DETAIL: Na 140, K 3.9, Cr 1.0, glucose 112, troponin <0.01, INR 1.0.

brain_ct_noncontrast.summary: IMAGING-FINDING: Subtle hyperdensity along the right Sylvian fissure consistent with acute subarachnoid blood; no midline shift; no hydrocephalus.

brain_mri.summary: IMAGING-FINDING: Not indicated as first-line in this presentation. Susceptibility-weighted sequences would confirm CT findings if obtained but should not be ordered before CT.

carotid_ultrasound.summary: IMAGING-FINDING: Not indicated for this presentation; carotid duplex does not evaluate intracranial bleeding.

neurology.default_question: Is non-contrast head CT sufficient to rule in or out subarachnoid hemorrhage at 90 minutes post-onset?
neurology.impression: Non-contrast CT within 6 hours of onset has >95% sensitivity for SAH. If CT positive, page neurosurgery for CTA and ICU admission. If CT negative and clinical suspicion remains, lumbar puncture is the next step, not additional imaging.
neurology.recommended_next_step: Order non-contrast head CT first; do not order MRI or ultrasound concurrently. Page neurosurgery if CT positive.

HC-SA-006.objective: Reconcile a complex polypharmacy regimen on hospital discharge for an elderly patient with CHF, AF, and CKD.
HC-SA-006.demographics: PATIENT-DEMOGRAPHICS: 74-year-old female, history of HFrEF (EF 32%), AFib on warfarin, CKD stage 3a, T2DM.
HC-SA-006.opening_summary: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Discharged today after 5-day hospitalization for decompensated heart failure. Recent additions of amiodarone and azithromycin overlap with chronic warfarin and digoxin therapy. Renal function declined from baseline during admission.
HC-SA-006.correct_diagnosis: High-risk polypharmacy with warfarin-amiodarone interaction, digoxin toxicity risk in renal decline, and metformin contraindication at current eGFR; reconciliation requires a single comprehensive history review plus renal panel before issuing the assessment.
HC-SA-006.recommended_service: Clinical pharmacy with cardiology medication review
HC-SA-006.urgency: Discharge today — reconciliation must be completed before patient leaves

histories.medications: MEDICATION-HISTORY: Warfarin 5 mg daily (INR 2.4 on admission, 4.1 today), Amiodarone 200 mg daily started day 2 of admission, Digoxin 0.125 mg daily, Furosemide 40 mg BID, Metformin 1000 mg BID, Lisinopril 10 mg daily (held during admission), Azithromycin 250 mg daily x3 days remaining, Atorvastatin 40 mg nightly.
histories.present_illness: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Resolution of pulmonary edema, weight down 4 kg from admission. Complains of mild nausea and one episode of palpitations overnight.
histories.past_medical_history: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: HFrEF with EF 32% (echo 6 months ago). AFib diagnosed 3 years ago, CHA2DS2-VASc 5. CKD stage 3a (baseline Cr 1.4). T2DM on metformin and sitagliptin (sitagliptin held during admission).
histories.social_context: SYMPTOM-HISTORY: Lives alone; daughter visits weekly. Self-administers medications using a weekly pillbox. No tobacco; remote alcohol use.

physical_exams.general_exam: EXAM-FINDING: BP 118/68, HR 72 irregular, RR 14, SpO2 95% on room air. JVP 8 cm. Trace bilateral pedal edema (improved from 3+).
physical_exams.renal_exam: EXAM-FINDING: No flank tenderness; bladder non-distended. Skin turgor adequate.

renal_function.summary: LAB-DETAIL: Cr 1.9 (baseline 1.4), eGFR 28 mL/min (down from 44), BUN 38, K 4.7, Na 136.

digoxin_level.summary: LAB-DETAIL: Digoxin 2.4 ng/mL (toxic threshold >2.0 in elderly with reduced renal clearance).

cardiology.default_question: How should warfarin and digoxin be adjusted given supratherapeutic INR, elevated digoxin level, and acute renal decline?
cardiology.impression: Hold warfarin x2 doses, recheck INR in 48 hours and resume at 60% prior dose. Hold digoxin and recheck level; do not restart until eGFR recovers above 35. Discontinue metformin at current eGFR; substitute linagliptin. Continue amiodarone for rhythm control but anticipate ongoing warfarin dose reduction.
cardiology.recommended_next_step: Update discharge medication list with hold/dose-reduction instructions; recheck INR and BMP within 72 hours; cardiology follow-up in 1 week.
